items.claim: `heldIndex` didn't truncate a fractional index, so `moveLayer` to its own slot recorded an undo entry
items.note: This also covers `addLayer`, `addPage` and `movePage`, which use the same helper.

items.claim: `reorder` with no index: its no-op check read it as the end, its payload as the start
items.note: It now means the end in both places, as `move` has it.

items.claim: `loadState` with a journal open left that journal holding the replaced document's ops
items.note: I made the strict call: it now throws while any journal is open, suspended ones included. Recorded in `docs/unruled.md` under a new "Audit round forty-one" section. It changes behavior: the changeset is tagged `fix behavior`.

items.claim: stale replay never skipped layer ops, so a layer removed by an untracked edit left undo entries that threw on every step
items.note: That covers `kit:setLayerVisible`, `kit:setLayerLocked`, `kit:setLayerParallax`, `kit:renameLayer` and `kit:moveLayer`. It also covers B's sub-cases: `kit:setLayer`, a `kit:add` onto a missing layer, and a `kit:remove` restored onto one. It also covers `kit:addLayer`/`kit:removeLayer` when the layer is already there or already gone.

items.claim: `freshIds` could mint an id that a restored history brings back
items.note: Ids that a `restoreHistory` snapshot adds or removes now count as taken. The set is replaced on each restore and emptied by `history.clear` and `loadState`, so it never grows past one snapshot.

items.claim: a reverted `kit:remove` dropped the nodes' pose previews and scroll offsets
items.note: Forgetting now waits until the edit settles, and only for nodes still gone. My test covers a batch that throws. For a refused arrival I'm inferring rather than testing: that path also runs inside a held notice, so it should behave the same.

items.claim: removal by stale index : undoing `addLayer`, and redoing `removeLayer`, took out the layer at the recorded index. After an untracked `moveLayer`, that removed a different layer
items.note: both now find the layer by id.
